adhd.label: Step 1 · Ch. 1–2: Fast System 1 vs. Effortful System 2 (Start Here)
adhd.brief: Introduces the two actors inside your brain: automatic System 1 that builds instant visual movies, and lazy, energy-protective System 2 that avoids heavy cognitive load.

adhd.label: Step 2 · Jumps to Part V (Ch. 35–36): The Experiencing Self vs. The Remembering Self
adhd.brief: Jumps to Kahneman's deepest life insight: why the self that lives in the present moment is completely different from the storyteller self that judges experiences only by their peak and their ending.

adhd.label: Step 3 · Jumps Back to Part IV (Ch. 26): Prospect Theory & Loss Aversion
adhd.brief: Unpacks the Nobel Prize discovery of why losing ₹1,000 triggers twice as much gut pain as winning ₹1,000 brings joy, and how reference points govern human risk.

adhd.label: Step 4 · Jumps Back to Part I (Ch. 5): Cognitive Ease & Why Familiarity Feels True
adhd.brief: Shows how clear typography, simple language, and a calm mood put System 1 into 'Cognitive Ease,' lowering your guard and making everything feel effortless and true.

adhd.label: Step 5 · Jumps to Part II (Ch. 11 & 17): Anchoring & Regression to the Mean
adhd.brief: Reveals how arbitrary numbers silently hijack negotiations and why unusually good or bad days naturally revert toward average without needing a causal story.
